name: Banquet & Wedding Buffet
headline: Three hundred covers, one line, no cold food.
intro: A wedding buffet is a logistics problem dressed as a design problem. The metal has to hold heat for two hours, survive being loaded by staff who are moving fast, and photograph well in a room lit for people rather than for food.
scenario: A 300-cover reception with a twelve-metre buffet line, live counters at both ends and a dessert island in the centre.
what_to_specify: Roll-top chafers along the main line — servers pass in one direction and never lift a lid.
One soup station per 100 covers, positioned at the head of the line where the queue forms.
Graduated risers under the cold section so the line has a horizon rather than a flat run.
Charger plates on the seated tables in a finish that answers the chafers, not the linen.

name: Fine Dining Table Setting
headline: The metal a guest touches before the food arrives.
intro: At a covered table the metalware is doing its work during the ten minutes before service — the charger, the napkin ring, the water pitcher. It is the room's first statement about price.
scenario: A 60-cover restaurant setting for dinner service, white linen, low warm light.
what_to_specify: A charger plate with a reveal of 12–18 mm around your dinner plate.
Antique or satin finishes under warm light; mirror finishes under cool light.
Matching napkin rings and menu holders — the cheapest coherence you can buy.

name: Poolside & Outdoor Brunch
headline: Sun, chlorine and salt air are a materials problem.
intro: Outdoors, finish decides lifespan. Lacquered brass chalks in direct sun, and mirror polish shows every water spot within an hour of a wipe-down.
scenario: A resort Sunday brunch on an open deck, 11am to 3pm, in direct sun.
what_to_specify: Stainless steel 304 or PVD-coated pieces for anything left in the sun.
Hammered faces over mirror — they hide water spotting between wipe-downs.
Double-wall coolers and insulated bowls, which do not sweat onto the cloth.
Weighted bases on anything tall enough for wind to take.

name: Room Service & In-Room Dining
headline: It travels a corridor, a lift and a threshold.
intro: In-room dining is the only service where the metalware is carried further than it is looked at. Non-slip surfaces and a cloche that seals are worth more here than any decorative detail.
scenario: A 180-key hotel running in-room dining from a single kitchen floor.
what_to_specify: Non-slip butler trays with a raised gallery rim.
Cloches that sit dead flat and do not ring when set down.
Insulated pieces — the food is plated eight minutes before the guest sees it.

name: Bar & Lounge
headline: Metal under low light, handled all night.
intro: Bar metal is handled more than any other category in a hotel, by wet hands, at speed. It is also the most visible: a shaker is worked at eye level, eighteen inches from a paying guest.
scenario: A 40-seat hotel lounge bar, low warm light, cocktail-led programme.
what_to_specify: Copper and antique brass, which read warm under low light where steel reads clinical.
Non-slip bar trays — the single most-replaced item behind any bar.
Ice buckets with a drain insert if the bar serves bottles at the table.

name: Breakfast Buffet & Live Counter
headline: Four hours, continuous refill, one attendant.
intro: Breakfast is the longest continuous service in a hotel and the one guests judge most consistently. Everything on the counter is refilled while guests are standing at it.
scenario: A 120-key business hotel serving breakfast 6:30–10:30, egg counter live.
what_to_specify: Split-pan mini chafers for condiments and sides — refilled without closing the station.
A juice dispenser with a stand rather than jugs; jugs are a labour cost.
A tiered stand for pastry, which halves the counter length you need.

name: Home Entertaining
headline: Hotel metal, domestic scale.
intro: The same pieces, bought one or two at a time. A copper handi on a dining table at home is doing exactly what it does in a hotel — it is simply not being washed forty times a week.
scenario: A dinner for eight at home, served family-style from the table.
what_to_specify: Copper handis and hammered platters, which go from oven to table.
One good tray. It becomes the piece you use most and think about least.
Lacquered brass indoors — it does not need the weekly polish that raw brass does.
